summary: The run’s main failure was an HP-economy problem established well before the Slime Boss fight. Optional HP-cost events and a later smith left the run entering the boss at only 35 HP, so the final combat began from a highly fragile state despite a reasonably developed deck.

lessons.title: Do not buy optional rewards with critical HP
lessons.situation: When already below full HP and several combats remain before the boss, evaluate HP-cost events as a major combat resource rather than as free gold or upgrades.
lessons.lesson: Decline optional HP-loss events unless their reward is essential to the run’s immediate survival plan. The gold from Gather Gold and the random upgrades from Enter were not worth repeatedly reducing the HP buffer before the boss.
evidence_points: At Floor 4, HP was 68/80 and Gather Gold was chosen, reducing HP to 57/80.
At Floor 5, HP was 57/80 and Enter was chosen, reducing HP to 41/80.
After those choices, combat logs reached 29/80 at Floor 6 and 24/80 at Floor 7.
lessons.reasoning: The two optional events removed 27 HP before later fights, and the subsequent combat losses left the run dependent on scarce healing. This made the later boss approach much less forgiving.

lessons.title: Prioritize a second heal when the boss approach is fragile
lessons.situation: At a campfire before the Act 1 boss, if HP remains substantially below maximum after an earlier rest and there are no saved potions, healing is usually more valuable than a marginal upgrade.
lessons.lesson: After recovering from a low-HP route, continue healing at the next available campfire when the upcoming combats are still likely to consume the buffer. Do not automatically smith at around half HP when the boss is close.
evidence_points: Floor 8 used a rest at 24/80 HP and recovered to 48/80.
At Floor 10, with 48/80 HP, smith was chosen instead of rest and Bash was upgraded.
The run then reached the Floor 15 rest at 11/80, recovered only to 35/80, and entered the Slime Boss combat at 35/80.
lessons.reasoning: The smith produced an upgrade, but the following fights reduced HP far faster than the run could recover. The final boss therefore started with only 35 HP and died after reaching a 7-HP state, indicating that preserving a larger pre-boss HP buffer was more urgent than the additional upgrade.
